A TCP SYN Flood attack works by exploiting the TCP handshake process. In this type of denial of service (DoS) attack, an adversary sends a large number of SYN (synchronize) requests to a target server, often using spoofed IP addresses. The server responds to each SYN request with a SYN-ACK (synchronize-acknowledge) packet, expecting a final ACK (acknowledge) packet to complete the handshake. However, since the source IP addresses are spoofed, the server never receives the final ACK, leading to half-open connections that consume server resources. This can overwhelm the server, reducing its availability and functionality [Source 1].
